column1: # SOUP register — IEC 62304 §5.3.3 / §8.1.2, ISO/IEC 27001 A.8 supply chain
# Every *direct* dependency of this crate must appear here with a purpose
# and a safety/security relevance note. `src/compliance/soup.rs` merges
# these annotations with the real dependency graph from Cargo.lock to
# produce the CycloneDX SBOM at GET /api/compliance/sbom, and its unit
# tests fail the build when a direct dependency is missing (or when an
# entry names a package that is no longer depended on).
# Scope note: this service is a **workforce identity registry**. It
# holds personal data and serves a FHIR `Practitioner` representation,
# and it additionally stores aptitude / personality / psychometric /
# selection assessment results per worker — employment-consequential
# data whose disclosure can cost someone a job. It is not a medical
# device: no output drives an individual's treatment (the qualification
# therefore carries no IEC 62304 safety classification, and
# GET /api/compliance says so rather than leaving it inferred.
# "Safety relevance" below means relevance to the correctness and
# confidentiality of personal data, not to physical safety.
# Transitive dependencies are listed in the SBOM but are NOT individually
# annotated. Stating that boundary is more honest than implying we have
# Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored.

column2: Async runtime.
column3: Availability-relevant. Runtime failure means unavailability, not disclosure. Industry standard.

column2: HTTP server, extractors, routing, and response types.
column3: SECURITY-RELEVANT. Header and path extraction feed the auth guard and the disclosure-audit context; a routing defect could reach a handler the guard believed it had covered.

column2: Middleware composition for the service stack.
column3: Security-relevant. The blanket auth guard is a layer in this stack; ordering determines whether it runs before a handler.

column2: CORS, compression, and tracing layers.
column3: Security-relevant. CORS configuration decides which origins may make credentialed calls to this API.

column2: Serialization framework for every wire type and stored payload.
column3: Security-relevant. A mis-serialized payload could corrupt a stored person record or an audit snapshot.

column2: JSON encoding/decoding, and the canonical form the audit hash chain digests.
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Key ordering (BTreeMap; preserve_order disabled) is load-bearing for chain verification across a JSONB round-trip. A reordering would report untouched rows as tampered — a false accusation is as damaging as a missed one.

column2: Async ORM and query builder over PostgreSQL.
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. All persistence, including the audit trail, the erasure sweep, and record-level authorization reads. Query construction uses its typed builders, not string concatenation, which is what keeps SQL injection out of the search paths.

column2: Exact decimal values in the persistence layer (src/db/models.rs).
column3: Not security-relevant. Arbitrary-precision arithmetic avoids float rounding in stored numerics; no identity or authorization decision depends on it.

column2: Web application framework: boot, routing, config, background workers, model error types.
column3: SECURITY-RELEVANT. Owns the boot sequence and the middleware stack, so a defect could bypass the auth/ABAC guard.

column2: This crate's own sea-orm-migration migrator (path dependency).
column3: Security-relevant. Owns the schema, including the audit_logs compliance columns and entity_links. First-party code, not third-party SOUP.

column2: Embedded full-text search index over worker records.
column3: SECURITY-RELEVANT. Holds a searchable copy of personal data outside PostgreSQL, so it is a second place masking and retention must be honoured — an erased record still present in the index is a live disclosure. Query paths take length-capped input (SEC-M1).

column2: gRPC transport for the real WorkerService server (PRO-H11, main dependency, 0.12) — Create/Get/List/Delete Worker, spawned alongside the REST router in App::after_routes; also resolved, at 0.14, from the renamed dev-dependency `otlp-test-tonic = { package = "tonic" }` serving tests/otlp_collector/'s in-process OTLP collector (PRO-H9) — Cargo.lock carries both versions as separate `tonic` packages under this one register row.
column3: SECURITY-RELEVANT. A second live API surface: src/api/grpc/service.rs runs the same blanket-enforcement + record-level ABAC decision REST makes (grpc_enforce / auth::authorize_record), gated by the same WORKER_REQUIRE_AUTH flag, so enabling enforcement protects both surfaces together, not REST alone. The 0.14 test-only resolution carries no production risk.

column2: Protobuf wire (de)serialization for the generated WorkerService messages (build.rs, tonic-build 0.12 codegen).
column3: Not security-relevant on its own — a message-encoding library, not an auth/authorization decision point. Malformed input still reaches crate::validation::validate_worker before persistence, same as a REST-decoded body.

column2: OpenAPI 3 document generation from handler annotations.
column3: Not security-relevant. Produces documentation; the served document names endpoints but discloses no record data.

column2: Serves the Swagger UI assets.
column3: Not security-relevant. Static documentation assets. The UI path is on the guard's public allow-list by design.

column2: Metrics and trace API (src/observability).
column3: Security-relevant. Span and metric attributes must not carry personal data or credentials; that is enforced at call sites, not by this crate.

column2: OTLP exporter for traces and metrics.
column3: SECURITY-RELEVANT. Ships telemetry off-box to a collector, so anything mistakenly placed in a span attribute leaves the trust boundary through it.

column2: Tracer/meter provider implementation and batching.
column3: Security-relevant. Same disclosure surface as the exporter it feeds.

column2: Standard attribute-name constants.
column3: Not security-relevant. Constants only.

column2: Structured logging and spans, including the audit_checkpoint witness lines.
column3: SECURITY-RELEVANT. The no-secrets-in-logs invariant is enforced at call sites, not by this crate. Checkpoint witness lines are emitted here, so a log pipeline that drops them silently removes the external-witness control.

column2: Log formatting, filtering, and the JSON layer.
column3: Security-relevant. Misconfiguration could emit more detail than intended; log level is deployment-controlled.

column2: Bridges tracing spans into OpenTelemetry.
column3: Security-relevant. Carries span fields across into exported telemetry, extending the log-hygiene requirement to the OTLP path.

column2: Public record identifiers (pid) and EntityRef ids.
column3: SECURITY-RELEVANT. v4 generation uses the OS RNG; a guessable pid would weaken the record-level authorization posture, since an id is the only thing standing between a caller and an object reference.

column2: Timestamps and the microsecond truncation the audit chain depends on.
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Chain digests bind created_at as epoch microseconds; a precision change would break verification of every existing row.

column2: Timestamps in the relay and bulk job paths.
column3: Security-relevant. Second time crate alongside chrono, a wart worth removing; both feed timestamps that appear in audit and outbox rows.

column2: Typed error enums (src/error.rs).
column3: Security-relevant. Error variants determine the HTTP status a failure maps to, including the 401/403 split that must not leak whether a record exists.

column2: Loads .env in development (src/config).
column3: Security-relevant. Reads configuration including secret material in dev; production configuration comes from the environment, not a file.

column2: Async methods in traits (repository and matcher seams).
column3: Not security-relevant. Compile-time macro only, no runtime behaviour of its own.

column2: Jaro-Winkler and Levenshtein string similarity (src/matching/algorithms.rs).
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Drives probabilistic identity matching. A false match merges two workers' records, including their assessment results — a confidentiality failure, not merely a data-quality one. Input is length-capped (SEC-M1) because the algorithms are O(n·m).

column2: Metrics registry and text-exposition rendering for /metrics.prom.
column3: Not security-relevant. Counters only; the endpoint exposes no record data and is on the public allow-list for scrapers.

column2: SHA-256 for the tamper-evident audit hash chain, record content hashes, and the worker_assessments digests.
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The integrity evidence for HIPAA §164.312(c) rests on this implementation. RustCrypto, widely audited; constant-time is not required for an unkeyed hash.

column2: Second integrity digest alongside SHA-256 for the audit chain and record hashes.
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Kept for structural diversity: SHA-3 is a sponge construction, unrelated to SHA-256's Merkle-Damgard chaining, so a cryptanalytic advance against one design family does not transfer. FIPS 202, so it carries NIST standing while being structurally independent of SHA-2. RustCrypto, same maintainers as sha2.

column2: Keyed integrity MACs (HMAC-SHA256) with HKDF domain separation, key sourcing, zeroization, and key generation (path dependency).
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The MAC is the only stored integrity value an adversary holding just the database cannot forge — the SHA-256 and SHA-3 digests are unkeyed with published pre-image formats. Extracted into one shared crate rather than copied per service precisely because a key-handling defect in a copy would not announce itself: it would make MACs forgeable while every test stayed green. First-party code with its own test suite, including golden vectors cross-checked against an independent HKDF implementation.

column2: Canonical matching engine and domain types (path dependency).
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. A false match conflates two workers, merging one person's employment and assessment history into another's. First-party code with its own spec, property tests, and no-IO posture.

column2: Cross-service EntityRef URN and EdgeKind registry for the same_identity (worker to person) edge (path dependency).
column3: SECURITY-RELEVANT. Edge-kind validation is what stops an arbitrary edge type being written into entity_links; the URN format is what the link-graph aggregator resolves. Worker's symmetric write side is still a follow-up, so today this is contract only.

column2: Offline PASETO v4.public verification and the shared ABAC policy engine (path dependency).
column3: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Every authentication and authorization decision depends on it, including record-level checks and masking obligations. First-party code with its own forgery and policy-property test suites.

column2: Real-broker durable-bus relay sink (BUS-3, src/relay.rs FluvioSink; ported from the case-service BUS-1 reference). Optional, behind this crate's own `fluvio` Cargo feature (off by default) — a default build carries none of it.
column3: Security-relevant when the feature is enabled. Ships the canonical event envelope (which can carry worker-linked personal data, including assessment results) to an external broker over the network; the relay never sends an entity's committed change without its outbox row, but a defect here could misroute or drop events reaching downstream consumers. Not present in a default release artefact.

column2: Global allocator for MUSL static builds.
column3: Availability-relevant. An allocator defect would be a process-wide fault. Enabled only for the musl target, through a cfg-gated global allocator.

column2: Serialises tests that mutate process-wide environment variables.
column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.

column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact; the test seed is not a secret.

column3: Test-only in this crate. The production verification path lives in authentication-verifier.

column3: Test-only. Not present in a release artefact.
